label: DERIVED -- our arithmetic on official results, not an official NBA statistic.
method: Rest is days since that team's previous game in the official log. Error is actual home margin minus our predicted home margin. Permutation p-values are two-sided with 20000 shuffles, seed 20261114. Multiple comparisons across the five tests are controlled with Benjamini-Hochberg at q < 0.05.

power.method: Two-sided test on a Pearson r, alpha 0.05, 80% power, using the effect size actually observed. It answers 'how much more data before this is worth re-testing', not 'is the effect real'.

question: Does our originated line already price rest, or does its error still carry a rest signal that a bettor could harvest?

tests.question: Rest differential (home rest - away rest) vs the originated line's margin error
tests.reading: A non-zero slope is points of margin error per extra day of home rest. If the line already prices rest, this is zero.

tests.question: Same test on the baseline (constant home-court margin) -- control
tests.reading: The baseline knows nothing about rest, so this is what 'unpriced rest' looks like. It is the yardstick for T1.

tests.question: Mean margin error when the away team is on a back-to-back and the home team is rested, vs every other game
tests.reading: If the model over-rates a rested road team the mean error here is negative. This is the subgroup a bettor would actually bet.

tests.question: Combined rest (home + away) vs the originated total's error
tests.reading: Tired teams scoring less is the theory. If the totals model ignores it, this shows up here.

tests.question: Walk-forward: would adding a rest term have reduced out-of-sample margin error? (coefficient fitted on earlier games only)
tests.reading: The coefficient is re-fitted before every game using only games already played, so a positive improvement is achievable in real time. A negative improvement means the rest term is noise that would have made the line worse.

verdict: The originated line does not price rest, and the rest signal shows up in its error in the expected direction: +2.44 points of home margin per extra day of home rest (r = 0.142, 95% CI -0.025 to 0.301, permutation p = 0.097, BH-adjusted q = 0.244 over five tests). In the classic spot -- rested home team against a road team on a back-to-back -- the home side beat our line by 8.4 points on average across 14 games. Neither survives correction for testing five hypotheses at once, and the walk-forward test settles it: fitting the rest coefficient on earlier games only and applying it forward made the line WORSE by 0.33 points of RMSE (16.01 to 16.34), with the coefficient swinging between -1.1 and 16.1 points per day as the sample grew. Conclusion: do not add a rest term on this evidence. Re-test when the out-of-sample sample reaches roughly 389 games.
